label: Entrostop, intact
scenario: Registered medicine, matching barcode, plausible weight.

label: Fatigon, no barcode
scenario: No barcode, so the machine relies on the photo alone. Accepted if the photo is confident enough.

label: Kalpanax, intact
scenario: Registered medicine, matching barcode, plausible weight.

label: Woods', intact
scenario: Registered medicine, matching barcode, plausible weight.

label: Promag, empty package
scenario: Weighs about the same as the empty package, so the medicine is used up.

label: Woods', filled with something heavy
scenario: Far heavier than a full package. The contents may have been swapped for a stone or similar.

label: Entrostop with a Fatigon barcode
scenario: The barcode belongs to another product, so it does not match the photo.

label: Kalpanax with an unregistered barcode
scenario: The barcode is not registered as a product in the machine.

label: Entrostop, slightly blurry photo
scenario: The photo is slightly blurry but the barcode matches. Confidence drops but stays above the pass mark.

label: Kalpanax, blurry photo, no barcode
scenario: Blurry photo and no barcode, so confidence falls below the photo-only pass mark.

label: Promag, very dark photo
scenario: The photo is too dark for the item to be recognized.

label: Plastic bottle with an Entrostop barcode
scenario: Registered barcode, but the item is junk. The barcode is only a claim; the photo shows it is not a medicine.

label: Doreta, a brand outside the dataset
scenario: A medicine the machine was not trained on, without a registered barcode.

label: Hair spray can
scenario: Pressurized cans are not accepted because they are a safety risk in the bin.
